newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany offers Peru aid for hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Germany offers Peru aid for hostage crisis.

text.p: Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Wednesday that Germany had offered Peru help in resolving the hostage crisis and he planned to appeal to Peru leaders to use prudence in their efforts to free the hostages.

Speaking to journalists in Bonn, Kinkel said he was trying to reach Peru President Alberto Fujimori on the telephone. Kinkel said he has been in contact with the foreign ministers of Japan and Austria.
"We expect and assume that Peru will do everything in its powers so that the lives of the hostages are not endangered," Kinkel said, adding he knows Fujimori personally.
Germany's ambassador to Peru is among at least 200 hostages held by heavily-armed guerrillas of the Cuban-inspired Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"I am extremely concerned and call on the hostage-takers to let the people free," Kinkel said.
Ambassador Heribert Woeckel was being held with around 15 other hostages in one room of the residence, Kinkel said.
Kinkel ordered Germany's ambassador to Bolivia to come to Lima and take over the running of the German embassy. A crisis specialist from Bonn was also en route to the Peruvian capital, Kinkel said.
"I will offer to send a group of experts from the federal crime office if that is desired," Kinkel said.
